camera.source: x: shots/ocean-sam/camera.json (phase correlation of the whole frame; the sea runs right about 217 px). y: the same up to frame 24, then the pitch read from the horizon itself (the bottom edge of the pale sky band, measured on every frame from 25 to 37, entering from above the top edge at frame 25), because phase correlation stalls at frames 28-31 while the horizon keeps dropping. Both smoothed (Gaussian, 1.5 frames) to remove uneven measurement steps. The camera turns on a ship, so near and far water shift alike on screen and every plane keeps z 2; depth.json's top band is sky and its middle band is empty.

planes.label: Horizon (camera turns, so it moves with the full measured camera)

objects.why: the horizon comes in from the top edge at frame 25 as the ship pitches; no Quick, Draw! category is a single level line, so it is one slightly uneven stroke, placed where the film's sky band ends; raised 12 px and shown from frame 29, so it enters whole at the top as the film's sky band comes into view, with no partial line before

notes.0: choppy open sea; the drawing holds roughly in place while its lines heave
notes.12: a big swell starts to build on the right
notes.25: the horizon enters at the top edge as the ship pitches up
notes.28: the crest breaks, its lip throws forward and down
notes.37: the swell has passed; the horizon sits above the drawing
